correctness.rationale: For every odd p, d_p=ord_p(b) divides p-1; the odd-prime lifting-the-exponent identity gives v_p(b^(d_p u)-1)=h_p+v_p(u). Thus ord_(p^a)(b)=d_p p^max(0,a-h_p), and L=ord_n(b) is the CRT lcm. The exact p-valuation of L equals max(max_q v_p(d_q), max(0,a_p-h_p)); hence v_p(b^L-1)=max(t_p,a_p) and the quotient valuation max(0,t_p-a_p). This proves all exponent bounds and the first power without a finite cutoff. Independent integer tests of modular quotient p-adic valuations in 2489 base/odd-modulus pairs corroborate; no claims for even moduli/noncoprime bases.
residual_risks: Even moduli and noncoprime bases excluded; no global counting density claimed.
